propositions: The reconciler's committed .bridge_state cache consumes 92% (≈950 MiB) of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch due to unchanged bookkeeping fields baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass that are written per-pass but not read by src code

Removing the timestamp baseline_advanced_at and moving last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping to a separate file reduces marginal packed cost per version from 12.79 KB to ≤3.2 KB (≤25% of baseline), enabling 8.4× compression of historical versions

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import pipeline reduces the existing tickets branch from 1.17 GiB to 99 MiB while preserving all 49,888 commits, 2,661 merges, and ensuring HEAD tree remains byte-identical to pre-rewrite tip

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners requiring durable state in git; the fix keeps .bridge_state committed while eliminating wasteful churn through write-when-changed guards and format normalization (description/status/priority as scalars, assignee as raw object)

Multi-version compatibility during rollout uses max(legacy, new) read logic and self-healing scrubbing; rollback is explicit and quiesced, restoring old branch tip only after bundle verification and all writers are reset to old-epoch clones

Epoch guard at sync._union_merge and push.py enforces fail-closed abort on version mismatch, eliminating resurrection risk post-rewrite; live review-bot and host-runtime epoch refusal proofs gate publication
